title: Fiddlers turned banjoists: Wyatt Houston and the roadhouse string trio
summary: Fiddlers moved to banjo; Levy forms a roadhouse trio with Wyatt Houston, Milt Hinton and himself, and they stampede the place.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: There were quite a few of you fiddlers around in the early years. Now you went to banjo, what happened to the rest of them? They tried to make it to the middle of the fiddle.

Wyatt Houston was one of them that was a classical fiddler that turned to jazz and he really could play it. He played all the Joe Van Nudie stuff. Is that so? And all the Eddie Saw's stuff. I tell you what we did, we had a job. The booking agent asked me, he says, can you get a little string band together? There's no piano in the roadhouse. We're out at 111th Street. I said, yes, I'll get you. So I got Milton Hinton. You know he's big in New York now. I got Milton Hinton. He was in school, still in school. He'd been trying to play a little fiddle. And I said, you never play a little fiddle with that bass fiddle. I said, ruin your hands, you can't do it. You just can't do it. And at that time I bought a tenor guitar, a real good tenor guitar, Viga. And it was a beautiful thing. I ripped the devil out of it, see. I got him Hinton on bass, myself on the little guitar, and Wyatt Houston on violin. We went out this roadhouse and stampeded the place. The man…
I remember when I go like when you had the trill.

The man went out, down the street, there was a roadhouse, two, three roadhouses close there, like a corner or something. Went down there and bought the other band from the other place to hear us. Wyatt played a tremendous jazz fiddle and double stops galore. I never heard about his playing jazz. I don't think… Never recorded it. Never recorded it, no. But he really could, he really… See, he was a graduate of the American Conservatory in violin.
He knew so much. In the wintertime.
